newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-RAIN FRUSTRATES ENGLAND IN TOUR OPENER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN FRUSTRATES ENGLAND IN TOUR OPENER.

text.p: England bowled out an Academy XI for 201 on Friday in the first match of their New Zealand tour, but rain forced the game to be abandoned.
England, fresh from a 3-0 one-day international drubbing from test minnows Zimbabwe, were deprived of valuable batting practice after the rain came down in the break between innings.
All five England bowlers took wickets in the one-day game but the Academy side recovered well from early trouble at 99 for five.
Craig McMillan hit an aggressive 58 and Greg Loveridge made 54, frustrating the tourists by featuring in a ninth wicket stand of 45 with Shayne O'Connor.

England dismissed the home side in the 41st over after morning showers reduced the contest to 46 overs a side. Fast-medium bowler Andrew Caddick claimed three for 44 including the wickets of both openers and Loveridge.
Pace bowler Dominic Cork, who missed the Zimbabwe leg of the tour and is vital to England's hopes in New Zealand, took one for 39 from his seven overs.
"The weather's done us once again, but at least it's given us a chance to have a bowl and give Dominic a good opportunity to get some overs under his belt," coach David Lloyd said.
England's next game is a four-dayer against a New Zealand Selection starting on Monday in Palmerston North.
